article_content: A picture of the popular Brazilian actress Juliana Paes climbing onto a roof, taken from the TV soap opera 'Gabriela,' recently became an internet sensation in Brazil. However, the image was doctored; instead of a kite, Paes is shown holding a smartphone, accompanied by the caption: 'I finally got a TIM signal!' This is an internet joke referencing widespread complaints from Brazilian consumers regarding the wireless carrier TIM's unreliable coverage. In a July survey on its Facebook page, the Rio de Janeiro-based technology review site TechTudo asked: 'Which mobile operator has the worst signal?' TIM, Brazil's second-largest cell phone company, received the most votes with 2,127, identifying it as the worst. Oi came in second with only 337 votes. Additionally, a spoof video featuring Brazilian comedian Fabio Porchat, wearing blue make-up and portraying someone struggling to cancel a TIM subscription, has garnered nearly three million views. The Blue Man Group, known for their trademark blue make-up, has previously created commercials for TIM in Brazil. Brazilian mobile network operators have faced increasing scrutiny from the Brazilian telecoms watchdog in recent months due to consumer complaints about poor service, including dropped calls and lack of signal. In July, the telecoms regulator Anatel prohibited three mobile operators from selling new cellphone plans in specific states, according to a report by telecoms market research firm TeleGeography. TIM, the Brazilian subsidiary of Telecom Italia, was banned in 19 states, Oi SA in five, and Telecom Américas (Claro) in three, as reported by TeleGeography. This ban was lifted in early August. Mobile subscription penetration in Brazil is at 131%, with 258 million mobile phone users out of a population of approximately 200 million. However, analysts have criticized operators for not investing in infrastructure during the mobile boom. The World Bank reports that 98% of Latin America's population now has a mobile phone signal, with Argentina and Panama experiencing significant subscription growth. Predictions made in 2013 suggested that by 2015, at least half of Brazil's population, or 100 million people, would have internet access on their mobile phones. (Note: This was a prediction from the original article and its accuracy would need to be verified). Blogger Anthony Hurtado believes that despite high mobile tariffs and excessive regulation, Brazil will soon experience a smartphone revolution. Meanwhile, the favelas, Brazil's informal settlements on the edges of urban areas characterized by overcrowding, lack of basic amenities and sanitation, and informal markets, have undergone their own mobile revolution—though not always legitimate. Similar to how they are havens for 'gatos' (illegal connections to water and electricity), they have become centers for selling stolen handsets and special SIM cards, known as 'diretão,' which allow free international calls for three months. According to 'Mobile Phone Appropriation in the Favelas of Rio de Janeiro,' published in New Media & Society, these are especially popular among drug barons. Approximately 20% of Rio de Janeiro's population lives in favelas, according to the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics, and there are over 6,000 favelas across Brazil in more than 300 cities. However, mobile technology has also been a positive force. The Brazilian NGO Viva Rio has been running the Viva Favela project since 2001. Starting with 20 community correspondents in Rio, it now has over 300 across Brazil who create text, photos, audio, and video about their lives, news, and cultural activities for its online magazine and website, which is read by favela residents. Editorial Coordinator of Viva Favela Viktor Chagas explains that cell phones have enabled residents who cannot read and write well to participate by submitting video stories and pictures created on their phones, at a low cost since the charity lacks funds to purchase camcorders. 'Cell phones are a massive platform of inclusion,' he says. 'With these new technologies, more people are producing culture, news, and content.' Guilherme Junior, 31, an arts teacher and correspondent for the site who lives in Bangu, Rio de Janeiro, explains: 'We have to make an extra effort to create positive news, as the newspapers always show only bad things about our communities.' Chagas adds, 'We have helped people perceive favelas differently, and we have helped favela dwellers identify themselves differently. Favelado had such a pejorative meaning in the 80s and 90s. Now the residents use their identity to strengthen their sense of belonging.' Viva Favela also trains residents to make films and take photographs on their cell phones. A photograph and audiovisual workshop held at the abandoned Cine Guaraci in Rocha Miranda, Rio, even inspired residents to start a successful campaign to reopen it, according to Chagas. The Alô Cidadão! (Hello Citizen!) project, which ran until 2009, allowed low-income residents, who often did not leave their favelas due to gang violence, to subscribe and receive free daily SMS messages about community news, job openings, vaccination drives, and cultural events. It was created by the non-profit Institute Hartmann Regueira (IHR) and funded by Oi Futuro, the social arm of the largest Brazilian telecommunications company Oi, and Spring Wireless. The content was sourced from local newspapers and partnerships with community groups and businesses. IHR is now exploring a new project with Oi using a smartphone application to combat bullying in schools in Belo Horizonte. Rede Jovem, another social project led by NGO Solidaritas, runs Mobile Rede Jovem: SMS for Social Change, which sends daily messages about job opportunities, cultural events, sports, courses, and free public services to members of poor communities. It also runs WikiMapa, a program in which favela residents, known as wiki-reporters, use GPS-enabled camera smartphones with a WikiMapa mobile application to map unregistered streets and add photos and videos of local points of interest, such as hospitals, churches, and stores. These are then uploaded to www.wikimapa.org.br. The project has mapped 29 favelas in Rio de Janeiro, funded by Fundación Telefónica, the social investment arm of the Brazilian wireless provider Vivo. Many slums and low-income areas do not appear on official online maps, so the initial goal was to add the narrow, winding, often-chaotic, unregistered streets of the favelas to virtual maps. This significantly impacted the favelados. Camila Santos, 26, a wiki-reporter and resident of the Complexo do Alemao favela, states, 'This is the only project that we have to identify and cast good things within one of the slums already considered as the most dangerous in Rio de Janeiro.' Natalia Santos, Executive Director of Rede Jovem, adds, 'The sense of marginalization after not even finding a reference to where they lived on virtual maps has been replaced by a twinkle in their eyes now that they can spot their streets and schools among many other used services locally available. The results are a strengthened sense of identity and increased self-esteem.'
translated_content: Et billede af den populære brasilianske skuespillerinde Juliana Paes, der klatrer op på et tag, taget fra tv-serien 'Gabriela', gik for nylig viralt i Brasilien. Billedet var dog manipuleret; i stedet for en drage holder Paes en smartphone, med teksten: 'Jeg har endelig fået et TIM-signal!' Det er en joke, der henviser til de mange klager fra brasilianske forbrugere over teleselskabet TIM's dårlige dækning. I en undersøgelse på Facebook i juli spurgte Rio de Janeiro-baserede TechTudo: 'Hvilket teleselskab har det dårligste signal?' TIM, Brasiliens næststørste mobilselskab, fik flest stemmer (2.127) og blev kåret som det værste. Oi kom på andenpladsen med kun 337 stemmer. En parodivideo med den brasilianske komiker Fabio Porchat, der er blåmalet og forsøger at afmelde et TIM-abonnement, er blevet set næsten tre millioner gange. Blue Man Group, kendt for deres blå ansigter, har tidligere lavet reklamer for TIM i Brasilien. Brasilianske teleselskaber er under pres fra de brasilianske telemyndigheder pga. klager over dårlig service, f.eks. afbrudte opkald og manglende signal. I juli forbød telemyndigheden Anatel tre selskaber at sælge nye mobilabonnementer i visse stater, ifølge TeleGeography. TIM (Telecom Italias datterselskab) blev forbudt i 19 stater, Oi SA i fem og Telecom Américas (Claro) i tre. Forbuddet blev ophævet i august. Mobildækningen i Brasilien er 131 %, med 258 millioner mobilbrugere ud af en befolkning på ca. 200 millioner. Analytikere kritiserer selskaberne for ikke at investere i infrastruktur under mobilboomet. Verdensbanken rapporterer, at 98 % af Latinamerikas befolkning nu har mobilsignal, især i Argentina og Panama. I 2013 forudså man, at mindst halvdelen af Brasiliens befolkning (100 millioner) ville have mobilinternet i 2015. (Det var en forudsigelse, hvis rigtighed bør undersøges). Bloggeren Anthony Hurtado mener, at Brasilien snart vil opleve en smartphone-revolution trods høje priser og regulering. Samtidig har favelaerne (Brasiliens slumområder) også oplevet en mobilrevolution, men ikke altid på lovlig vis. Ligesom de er kendt for ulovlige strøm- og vandforbindelser ('gatos'), er de også blevet et marked for stjålne mobiltelefoner og særlige SIM-kort ('diretão'), der giver gratis internationale opkald i tre måneder. De er populære blandt narkobaroner, ifølge en artikel om mobilbrug i favelaerne i Rio de Janeiro, udgivet i New Media & Society. Ca. 20 % af befolkningen i Rio de Janeiro bor i favelaer ifølge det brasilianske institut for geografi og statistik. Der er over 6.000 favelaer i Brasilien, fordelt på over 300 byer. Men mobilteknologi har også haft en positiv indvirkning. NGO'en Viva Rio har drevet projektet Viva Favela siden 2001. Det startede med 20 lokale journalister i Rio, men har nu over 300, der producerer tekst, fotos og video om deres liv og lokalområde til Viva Favelas magasin og hjemmeside. Viktor Chagas (redaktør på Viva Favela) forklarer, at mobiltelefoner har gjort det muligt for folk, der har svært ved at læse og skrive, at deltage ved at indsende videoklip og billeder. Det er billigt, da organisationen ikke har råd til kameraer. 'Mobiltelefoner er en platform for inklusion,' siger han. 'De nye teknologier giver flere mulighed for at producere kultur og nyheder.' Guilherme Junior (31, kunstlærer og journalist) forklarer: 'Vi skal gøre en ekstra indsats for at skrive positive historier, da aviserne kun fokuserer på det negative.' Chagas tilføjer: 'Vi har hjulpet folk med at se favelaerne på en ny måde, og vi har hjulpet beboerne med at definere sig selv. 'Favelado' var et skældsord i 80'erne og 90'erne. Nu bruger beboerne deres identitet til at styrke deres fællesskab.' Viva Favela lærer også beboerne at lave film og tage billeder med deres mobiltelefoner. En workshop på den nedlagte biograf Cine Guaraci inspirerede beboerne til at starte en kampagne for at genåbne den, og det lykkedes. Projektet Alô Cidadão! (Hej Borger!) gav lavindkomstborgere, der ofte ikke forlod deres favela pga. bandevold, mulighed for at abonnere på gratis SMS-beskeder om lokalområdet, job, vaccinationer og arrangementer. Det blev skabt af Institute Hartmann Regueira (IHR) og finansieret af Oi Futuro og Spring Wireless. Indholdet kom fra lokale aviser og samarbejder med lokale grupper og virksomheder. IHR undersøger nu et projekt med Oi, der bruger en app til at bekæmpe mobning i skoler i Belo Horizonte. Rede Jovem (et andet projekt under NGO'en Solidaritas) driver 'Mobile Rede Jovem: SMS for Social Change', der sender beskeder om job, arrangementer, sport, kurser og offentlige tjenester til udsatte borgere. Projektet WikiMapa bruger GPS-smartphones til at kortlægge uregistrerede gader i favelaerne og tilføje billeder og video af steder som hospitaler, kirker og butikker. Det uploades til www.wikimapa.org.br. Projektet har kortlagt 29 favelaer i Rio de Janeiro og er finansieret af Fundación Telefónica. Mange slumområder findes ikke på onlinekort, så målet var at tilføje de smalle, kaotiske gader i favelaerne. Det har haft stor betydning for beboerne. Camila Santos (26, journalist) siger: 'Det er det eneste projekt, der fokuserer på det positive i et af de farligste slumområder i Rio.' Natalia Santos (leder af Rede Jovem) tilføjer: 'Før følte beboerne sig marginaliserede, fordi de ikke kunne finde deres hjem på kort. Nu kan de se deres gader og skoler, og det har givet dem en stærkere identitet og et bedre selvværd.'

article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) -- Buddy Holly was posthumously honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on Wednesday, coinciding with what would have been the singer-songwriter's 75th birthday. 'It's never too late when you get a fantastic thing to happen,' his widow, Maria Elena Holly, told CNN after unveiling the star on Vine Street at the entrance to the historic Capitol Records building. Holly was only 22 years old when he tragically died in a plane crash, alongside fellow musicians Ritchie Valens and J.P. 'The Big Bopper' Richardson. During the ceremony, his widow stated, 'I'm saying now, my dear Buddy, you loved to go to the movies. You told me that one of your dreams was to write scores for movies and make your mark in Hollywood.' 'Well, my dear, half of your dream unfortunately did not come true, but the other half did come true with a beautiful star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame,' she added. Actor Gary Busey, who portrayed Holly in the 1978 film 'The Buddy Holly Story,' also attended the dedication. 'He's here right now,' Busey remarked. 'I feel his spirit in the air. It's beautiful.' When asked what Holly would be doing if he were still alive, Busey responded, 'Anything he wanted to. Scoring movies, helping people in different countries who are in trouble, like writing a song for them and taking it over there and singing it to them.' Busey is currently collaborating with T Bone Burnett on an album of Holly songs, which he plans to perform on tour. The Hollywood star ceremony was scheduled to align with this week's release of 'Listen to Me: Buddy Holly,' a tribute album featuring his songs performed by 16 artists, including Ringo Starr, Stevie Nicks, Brian Wilson, Jackson Browne, Chris Isaak, Linda Ronstadt, and Lyle Lovett. Phil Everly of the Everly Brothers, a contemporary of Holly, was also present at the dedication.

Holly var kun 22 år gammel, da han tragisk døde i et flystyrt sammen med musikerne Ritchie Valens og J.P. 'The Big Bopper' Richardson. 'Ja, min kære, halvdelen af din drøm gik desværre ikke i opfyldelse, men den anden halvdel gik i opfyldelse med en smuk stjerne på Hollywood Walk of Fame,' tilføjede hun. article_content: If you'd like to eat more vegetables but find peeling them a chore, there's a solution. A £9.95 gadget can speed up the process and reduce the risk of cutting your fingers. The Karoto, resembling an oversized pencil sharpener, peels vegetables like courgettes, carrots, cucumbers, and parsnips. Scroll down for a video demonstration. Designed by the Israel-based firm Monkey Business, the Karoto looks like a giant pencil sharpener and can peel any root vegetable, including carrots and parsnips, in about 30 seconds. Using the Karoto is simple: insert the vegetable and twist it against the blade to remove the skin. The resulting cucumber and courgette shavings can be used to garnish salads. Its creators claim this time-saving invention is safer than using a standard peeler or knife. Avichai Tadmor designed the Karoto for Monkey Business design studio in Israel. His team claims it can peel a carrot completely in under 30 seconds, saving time and providing salad decorations. Measuring 3 inches long and 2 inches wide, the Karoto can also sharpen carrots for presentation. Jenni Day, sales manager at Luckies, a London-based gift site that sells the Karoto in the UK, said: 'The Karoto is a fun, quirky gift that makes preparing dishes more interesting.' 'It makes peeling vegetables easy and works with long root vegetables like carrots, courgettes, parsnips, and cucumbers. The Karoto saves time and is a safer alternative to using traditional peelers and knives.' The Karoto comes in orange and black and costs £9.95. 'While it has restrictions for children's use, like many cutlery and kitchen gadgets, it's easier to use than other peeling methods.' 'It resembles a pencil sharpener and works similarly, peeling a carrot in about 30 seconds.' 'Besides speeding up peeling, it creates curls for decorating salads and other dishes.' The Karoto, costing £9.95 plus postage, is also sold by Prezzybox. Another recent time-saving kitchen device, the Yolkr, separates egg yolks from whites. It works like a pipette, sucking the yolk into an attached plastic case before releasing it whole. After cracking an egg into a bowl, the gadget sucks up the yolk into a wide-mouthed plastic nozzle when the rubber top is squeezed. It holds the yolk safely until use, then releases it with another squeeze. The Yolkr costs £18.

article_content: A mother of four, Donna Eastwood, 26, was found dead in a burnt-out car, just 18 months after her partner was shot dead. Eastwood's children are aged between eight months and five years old. She was murdered after a dispute at a party near her home on Friday night. It is believed she was stabbed before her killer attempted to conceal the crime by leaving her body in a car, which was then set ablaze on a remote country lane in Wilmington, Kent. Detectives questioned a 26-year-old man on suspicion of murder after her body was discovered at 6:20 a.m. on Saturday. Following a police search involving helicopters and ground teams, a man was arrested at 2:30 p.m. on Sunday. The arrest occurred after speculation on social media regarding the identity of the suspect, who was reportedly known to the victim. The dispute at the party allegedly began after a remark by Eastwood angered another attendee. Eastwood, from Dartford, had recently lost her partner and father of three of her children, Kevin McKinley, who was fatally shot last year. McKinley, 32, was shot with a 12-bore shotgun while his son was nearby in a parked car in February. Michaela Sargeant, 25, received an eight-year sentence for manslaughter for shooting McKinley during a dispute outside her Dartford home. Her partner, Lewis Wickenden, 26, was sentenced to five years for assisting an offender. After McKinley's death, Eastwood posted a tribute online expressing her love for him. Police stated that McKinley's death is not believed to be related to Eastwood’s murder. A family member of Eastwood expressed their grief and concern for her children, emphasizing the need for their care. Neighbors described Eastwood as a 'nice girl' who had a 'diabolical' life and highlighted the challenges faced by her mother in caring for the children. Floral tributes were left at the location where her body was found. A police spokesman stated that Eastwood’s death is considered an isolated, targeted attack, and there is no indication of a broader threat to the public. The police added that the offender and victim knew each other.

Eastwoods børn er i alderen otte måneder til fem år. Hun blev myrdet efter en strid ved en fest i nærheden af hendes hjem fredag aften. Det menes, at hun blev stukket ned, før hendes morder forsøgte at skjule forbrydelsen ved at placere hendes lig i en bil, som derefter blev sat i brand på en afsides landevej i Wilmington, Kent. Politiets efterforskere afhørte en 26-årig mand, der er mistænkt for mord, efter at hendes lig blev fundet kl. 6:20 lørdag morgen. Efter en politiindsats med helikoptere og hold på jorden blev en mand arresteret kl. 14:30 søndag. Anholdelsen skete efter spekulationer på sociale medier om identiteten på den formodede gerningsmand, der efter sigende kendte offeret. Striden ved festen startede angiveligt, efter at en bemærkning fra Eastwood gjorde en anden deltager vred. Eastwood, fra Dartford, havde for nylig mistet sin partner og faren til tre af sine børn, Kevin McKinley, som blev dræbt ved skud sidste år. McKinley, 32, blev skudt med en 12-kaliber haglbøsse, mens hans søn var i nærheden i en parkeret bil i februar. Michaela Sargeant, 25, blev idømt otte års fængsel for uagtsomt manddrab, fordi hun skød McKinley under en strid uden for hendes hjem i Dartford. Hendes partner, Lewis Wickenden, 26, blev idømt fem års fængsel for medvirken. Efter McKinleys død skrev Eastwood en hyldest online, hvor hun udtrykte sin kærlighed til ham. Politiet har udtalt, at McKinleys død ikke menes at have forbindelse til Eastwoods mord. Et familiemedlem til Eastwood udtrykte sin sorg og bekymring for hendes børn og understregede, at de har brug for hjælp og støtte. Naboer beskrev Eastwood som en 'sød pige', der havde et 'forfærdeligt' liv, og fremhævede de udfordringer, hendes mor stod over for med at passe børnene. Blomster blev lagt på det sted, hvor hendes lig blev fundet. En talsmand for politiet udtalte, at Eastwoods død betragtes som et isoleret, målrettet angreb, og at der ikke er noget, der tyder på, at offentligheden er i fare. Politiet tilføjede, at gerningsmanden og offeret kendte hinanden.

article_content: David Mccormack PUBLISHED: 17:59 EST, 8 November 2012 UPDATED: 18:09 EST, 8 November 2012 Voters in New Hampshire have elected Stacie Laughton, making her the first transgender person to serve in their state legislature. Laughton, 28, won a seat in the New Hampshire House of Representatives in Tuesday’s election. She is a trans woman, meaning she has a female gender identity and was assigned male at birth. Laughton hopes her victory will inspire others from the LGBT (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender) community to become more involved in mainstream politics. Laughton's victory has been called a ‘milestone’ by the Gay & Lesbian Victory Fund. 'My hope is that we’ll see more people in the community running, perhaps for alderman. Maybe in the next election, we’ll have a senator,' she told The (Nashua) Telegraph. While gender issues are a key concern for Laughton, she also wants to be seen as just another member on the House floor and someone who represents all people, regardless of their gender identification. 'This area of New Hampshire needed somebody like me,' she said, 'somebody who understands the complex issues that this district faces, somebody who understands what it's like to live with a lower income, somebody who knows the people in the area.' Laughton has been politically active since she was a teenager. She generally takes a liberal position on most issues but considers herself conservative on financial matters. Laughton's key issues include advocating for the homeless, those in low-income housing, and those with mental illnesses and physical disabilities. She also aims to strengthen the public school system. The Gay & Lesbian Victory Fund, which supports out LGBT candidates and political appointees, hailed the victory as a ‘milestone.’ Laughton promises to represent all people, regardless of their gender identification. 'This is a milestone for LGBT Americans, and an especially important achievement for the transgender community,' Denis Dison, the group's vice president, told BuzzFeed. 'We're working to make sure qualified trans candidates have the training and resources they need to run and win, and we're seeing more and more take advantage of our Candidate Training program.' Tuesday’s election saw a wave of historic results. New Hampshire became the first state with an all-female Congressional delegation, with women taking the governor’s office and the other two congressional seats, besides the one Laughton won. Tammy Baldwin celebrated her victory over Republican candidate Tommy Thompson in Wisconsin. Maine, Maryland, and Washington voters made their states the first to pass legalized gay marriage by a popular vote. Voters in Minnesota defeated a constitutional measure that would have banned gay marriage. Democrat Tammy Baldwin also became the nation’s first openly gay U.S. senator by winning in Wisconsin. In Iowa, voters decided to retain a State Supreme Court justice, David Wiggins, rejecting a campaign by the State Republican Party and other conservative forces to oust him because of his participation in the court’s unanimous ruling in 2009 allowing same-sex-marriage on equal protection grounds.

article_content: Their intricate designs and the sheer impressive size of them require meticulous planning and precise execution. And the resulting crop circle, while illegal and irritating to the farmer whose field has been targeted, is usually visually stunning. But while some crop circles are remembered for their perfect symmetry and unique patterns, others are slightly less impressive. A series of recent attempts at producing circles have been met with much derision by fans of the field art after they recently appeared in Wiltshire. Not very impressive: This image of a heart appeared in a field of crops in Cherhill, Wiltshire. Rubbish: The heart-shaped crop circle appeared in the fields below the Westbury White Horse in Wiltshire. How it should look: A slightly more impressive crop circle featuring a heart which appeared in a nearby field in Wiltshire in August 2000. Insiders say a number of top crop circle makers have quit following a clampdown by farmers and moved onto making sand circles, which are legal. In previous years, impressive crop circles have drawn thousands of tourists to southern England, and some believers who saw the circles as the work of aliens. But this year, visitors have been disappointed by just a handful of crude patterns such as a square, a heart, and a small, uneven circle. Former crop circle maker Matthew Williams, who has given up his hobby because he suffers from hay fever, said the lack of competition is driving down standards. He said: 'The problem is that the best 'croppies' have retired or moved onto something new, so there isn't any competition anymore.' 'They're all creative types, and without any friendly rivalry, many just can't be bothered.' 'All the best crop circles from the last few years have been made by only a handful of people, and they've all hung up their wooden boards now and moved onto pastures new.' Bizarre: The prankster's attempts at a crop circle in this Devizes field did not quite go to plan; it's difficult to make out what the shape is supposed to be. Poor effort: This attempt at a crop circle is one of 15 to have appeared across the county so far this year. A better attempt: This stunning crop circle appeared in nearby Calne in August 2000. Matt, 42, reckons the 15 less-than-impressive circles that have appeared this year were created by amateurs. In comparison, seasoned veterans had produced more than 50 by this time last year. He said: 'Julian Richardson, one of the best croppies ever, has moved on to making sand circles instead.' 'He wants to try something different, and I think he's fed up with believers trying to make money from his hobby – that he never made a penny for.' 'I've retired due to hay fever, and a couple of my peers have just given up as well; it's becoming too difficult.' 'The farmers are getting angrier, the believers are getting too demanding, and we're still not making any money.' Matt hit the headlines in 2006 when he became the first person ever to be convicted of criminal damage for creating a crop circle in a field of wheat. What is it? It's anyone's guess as to what the creator of this circle was trying to depict. It's a mystery: Even a close-up of the crop formation doesn't give any clues as to what it is supposed to be. More like it: Perhaps the creators of this year's formation were hoping to produce something a little like this image which appeared in Chilbolton, Wiltshire, in August 2000. He was caught after setting up a sting to debunk a Ufologist's claim that he could communicate with aliens and would get them to make a specific shape in a field. Farmers across Wiltshire and Hampshire are also fed up with crop circles and tourists looking to have an 'out-of-body experience' inside them. Some have taken the drastic step of mowing the formations out of their fields as soon as they appear. Dutch crop circle 'expert' Monique Klinkenbergh tried to set up a pass scheme to charge people to look at the circles and walk inside them. The £60 season ticket was intended to bring in revenue for farmers, but it has flopped after it allowed access to only two formations. Gone: It is thought that the people behind crop circles such as this one, which appeared at Calne in August 2000, have moved on to pastures new. Monique and two colleagues, Derek Viner and Charles Mallett, set up a crop circle information center at a garden center in Woodborough, Wiltshire. Matt added: 'Loads of the boys are quitting making them now, because it's being ruined by outsiders like Klinkenbergh who are trying to make money from our hobby.' 'We in the circle-making community are outraged that outsiders like Klinkenbergh would come in and take over, trying to interfere.' 'Farmers are sick to their back teeth too and are cutting more circles out of their fields than ever before; if it continues like this, then there won't be any circles at all next year.' 'It's such a shame, because myself and a lot of people have had a great deal of fun with crop circles over the years.'

article_content: Love letters scattered across the floor, a gown hanging in the bedroom, and black-and-white photos veiled in cobwebs create a scene reminiscent of a fairytale. However, this derelict dairy farm, nestled deep within the Welsh countryside, presents a real-life mystery. Known as the 'Red Dress Manor,' the house is brimming with personal artifacts, including a floor-length red satin dress and numerous love letters. Remarkably, there has been no sign of occupancy within its walls for the past 40 years. According to documents discovered by photographer Dan Circa, the house, located in Llanymynech near Shrewsbury, is named Calcott Hall and received Grade II* listed status in 1953. The red dress, featured in a photograph on the wall, was found hanging in an empty wardrobe, alongside other garments strewn across the floor. The manor's nickname originates from the woman in the red dress, Ellen Jones, who appears in various images throughout the house. Decades of abandonment are evident in the living room, where a thick layer of dust coats the floor. The reason for the scattered newspapers and notes remains unknown. The four-bedroom house, officially Calcott Hall, in Llanymynech, Powys, Mid Wales, achieved grade II* listed status in 1953, over two centuries after its initial construction as a dairy farm. Census records indicate that the owner, Ellen Jones, passed away in the early 1970s, leaving her home a forgotten relic amidst its leafy surroundings. Her possessions remain untouched since her departure. A series of evocative images captured by photographer Dan Circa now reveals the enigmatic manor, illustrating how generations had made it their home over centuries. The eerie dairy farm, 'Red Dress Manor,' has been decaying for decades, preserving letters and pictures seemingly untouched by time. A rusted 1970s Morris car sits in the garage adjacent to the main house, a vehicle that could fetch a considerable sum at auction today. The letters and photographs left behind reveal that a woman named Ellen Jones once resided there, the dust adding to the mystical quality of the clear, evocative shots. The building retains its original 1725 architecture, featuring heavy wood doors, stone floors, and high ceilings. Few have ventured onto the property since the 1970s. Crumbling walls, plants invading the ceilings, and torn curtains amplify the building's ethereal and timeless beauty. Handbags, ribbons, and clothing scattered throughout the house offer glimpses into the lives of the women who inhabited it years ago. Dust-covered glass bottles containing 19th-century cleaning products like turpentine and black lacquer resemble artworks as sunlight streams through cracked windows. Floral 1950s wallpaper peeling from the walls exposes the heavy stone used in the house's 1725 construction. After years of neglect, nature has reclaimed the space, with branches and leaves penetrating the ceilings and soil spilling from the fireplace onto a 1960s television. Mr. Circa, 28, from Manchester, stated, 'I heard stories of the manor and wanted to investigate for myself. The picture of a lady in a red dress and the presence of the actual red dress were particularly intriguing. I was curious to see what else lay inside. I felt like I was intruding, constantly expecting the owner to appear.' Delicate bottles of turpentine, black lacquer, and healing oil represent cleaning products from a bygone era, a stark contrast to today's plastic containers. A box of Daz alongside older cleaning products, 1950s curtains, and an 18th-century wooden window frame illustrate how this manor served as home to generations. Floral curtains and mismatched floral wallpaper frame the Welsh countryside through broken glass, while a lone shoe rests on the windowsill, creating a decorative yet mysterious scene. 'Upon ascending the stairs to the main bedroom, I opened the door and saw a photo of the lady in the red garment on her dressing table, surrounded by makeup and personal items. Turning to the left, I found the open wardrobe with the red dress hanging inside. It was an unsettling experience, as if someone were present. I initially thought it was her.' The window panes are shattered, the curtain is drawn across the room, and clothes are scattered about, but the reason for the inhabitants' departure remains unknown. Framed certificates reveal that the beautiful and elegant Ellen Jones also passed her county examinations at the Shropshire Congregational Union. Framed pictures lean against a typical 60s television, positioned before two small chairs with bags and pillows across the floor, and soil spilling from the fireplace, all contributing to the clutter. It is a moment in time frozen and preserved. The mustard walls and art deco ornaments hint at a long family history within the abandoned manor. Mr. Circa describes his project as an exploration of 'beauty in decay': 'The lady in the red dress has been identified as Ellen Jones through census records and personal letters. I am documenting items that someone once cherished. People are amazed by the pictures, particularly when they realize the abundance of personal belongings within the space.' Det er bemærkelsesværdigt, at der ikke har været tegn på beboelse inden for dets mure i de sidste 40 år. Ifølge dokumenter opdaget af fotografen Dan Circa er huset, der ligger i Llanymynech nær Shrewsbury, navngivet Calcott Hall og blev fredet som Grade II* i 1953. Den røde kjole, der er afbilledet på et fotografi på væggen, blev fundet hængende i et tomt klædeskab sammen med andet tøj, der lå spredt på gulvet. Herregårdens kaldenavn stammer fra kvinden i den røde kjole, Ellen Jones, som optræder på forskellige billeder rundt omkring i huset. Årtiers forladthed er tydelig i stuen, hvor et tykt lag støv dækker gulvet. Årsagen til de spredte aviser og noter er fortsat ukendt. Fireværelseshuset, officielt Calcott Hall, i Llanymynech, Powys, Mid Wales, blev fredet som Grade II* i 1953, mere end to århundreder efter dets oprindelige opførelse som en gård. Folketællingsregistre viser, at ejeren, Ellen Jones, døde i begyndelsen af 1970'erne, og efterlod sit hjem som en glemt relikvie midt i sine grønne omgivelser. Hendes ejendele har stået urørt siden. En række stemningsfulde billeder taget af fotografen Dan Circa afslører nu den gådefulde herregård og illustrerer, hvordan generationer har boet der gennem århundreder. Den uhyggelige gård, 'Red Dress Manor', har været i forfald i årtier og bevarer breve og billeder, der tilsyneladende er uberørte af tiden. En rusten Morris-bil fra 1970'erne står i garagen ved siden af hovedhuset; en bil, der kunne indbringe en betydelig sum på auktion i dag. Breve og fotografier, der er efterladt, afslører, at en kvinde ved navn Ellen Jones engang boede der, og støvet bidrager til de klare og stemningsfulde billeders mystiske kvalitet. Bygningen har stadig sin originale arkitektur fra 1725 med tunge trædøre, stengulve og højt til loftet. Få har besøgt stedet siden 1970'erne. Smuldrende vægge, planter, der vokser ind gennem lofterne, og iturevne gardiner forstærker bygningens æteriske og tidløse skønhed. Håndtasker, bånd og tøj spredt rundt omkring i huset giver et indblik i de kvinders liv, der boede der for mange år siden. Støvdækkede glasflasker med rengøringsmidler fra det 19. århundrede, som terpentin og sort lak, ligner kunstværker, når sollyset strømmer ind gennem de revnede vinduer. Blomstret tapet fra 1950'erne, der skræller af væggene, afslører de tunge sten, der blev brugt i husets konstruktion i 1725. Efter mange års forsømmelse har naturen taget over med grene og blade, der trænger ind i lofterne, og jord, der spilder ud af pejsen på et fjernsyn fra 1960'erne. Hr. Circa, 28, fra Manchester, sagde: 'Jeg hørte historier om herregården og ville selv undersøge den. Billedet af damen i en rød kjole, og at selve den røde kjole stadig var der, var særligt spændende. Jeg var nysgerrig efter at se, hvad der ellers var indeni. Jeg følte, at jeg var trængte mig på, og forventede hele tiden, at ejeren ville dukke op.' Sarte flasker med terpentin, sort lak og helbredende olie er rengøringsmidler fra en svunden tid, en skarp kontrast til nutidens plastikbeholdere. En kasse Daz sammen med ældre rengøringsmidler, gardiner fra 1950'erne og en trævinduesramme fra det 18. århundrede illustrerer, hvordan denne herregård var hjem for generationer. Blomstrede gardiner og forskelligt blomstret tapet indrammer det walisiske landskab gennem knust glas, mens en ensom sko ligger i vindueskarmen og skaber en dekorativ, men mystisk scene. 'Da jeg gik op ad trappen til hovedsoveværelset, åbnede jeg døren og så et foto af damen i den røde kjole på hendes toiletbord omgivet af makeup og personlige ejendele. Da jeg vendte mig mod venstre, så jeg det åbne klædeskab med den røde kjole hængende derinde. Det var en urovækkende oplevelse, som om der var nogen til stede. Jeg troede først, at det var hende.' Vinduesruderne er knuste, gardinet er trukket for, og tøjet ligger spredt rundt omkring, men årsagen til beboernes afrejse er stadig ukendt. Indrammede certifikater viser, at den smukke og elegante Ellen Jones også bestod sine eksaminer i Shropshire Congregational Union. Indrammede billeder står op ad et typisk 60'er-fjernsyn foran to små stole med tasker og puder på gulvet, og jord, der spilder ud af pejsen, hvilket alt sammen bidrager til rodet. Det er et øjeblik i tiden, der er frosset fast og bevaret. De sennepsfarvede vægge og art deco-ornamenter antyder en lang familiehistorie i den forladte herregård. Hr. Circa beskriver sit projekt som en udforskning af 'skønhed i forfald': 'Damen i den røde kjole er blevet identificeret som Ellen Jones gennem folketællingsregistre og personlige breve. Jeg dokumenterer genstande, som nogen engang værdsatte. Folk er forbløffede over billederne, især når de ser, hvor mange personlige ejendele der er i rummet.' article_content: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was expected to be confirmed as the new manager of Cardiff City on Thursday afternoon. He was seen at the Emirates Stadium before Cardiff's match against Arsenal, watching their 2-0 defeat from the directors' box after arriving in London on owner Vincent Tan's private plane. The club hoped to officially name Solskjaer as Malky Mackay's replacement before their FA Cup tie against Newcastle this weekend [verify and specify date]. Sir Alex Ferguson, Solskjaer's former manager at Manchester United, reportedly advised him to avoid the club and Tan after three months of turmoil culminated in Mackay's departure last Friday. However, sources indicate that Cardiff chairman Mehmet Dalman held further discussions with the Molde manager’s representatives, seemingly convincing him to move to South Wales despite his initial reservations. Solskjaer is a patron of the Manchester United Supporters' Trust, which opposed the Glazer regime. During his tenure, the 40-year-old led Molde to two Norwegian titles (2011 and 2012) and a Norwegian Cup victory last year. Dalman had also been authorized by Tan to offer a significant January transfer budget, potentially extending to ‘whatever it takes to secure survival,’ according to a source close to Tan [unnamed source]. Reports from Norway suggest that Solskjaer, who is contracted until July, had not yet committed to leaving Molde. Egil Olsen is the only other Norwegian to have managed in the Premier League, a tenure that ended unhappily when Wimbledon was relegated in 1999. Two other Norwegians have managed in the Championship: Henning Berg, who lasted only 57 days at Blackburn, and Stale Solbakken, whose time at Wolves was considered a disaster. Tarje Nordstrand Jacobsen, the club's CEO at Molde stated: 'Ole Gunnar did not leave us a message about it one way or the other. He is still our manager, at least until the summer.' He declined to comment on reports that Solskjaer would be presented as the new Cardiff boss. Former Norway striker Jan Aage Fjortoft expressed disbelief on Twitter, stating that Solskjaer's move to Cardiff would contradict his previously stated principles. He had previously said Solskjaer would prioritize the club owner when choosing a team and therefore would not choose Cardiff. Paul Ince and Dan Petrescu had been considered as alternative options if Solskjaer declined the job. Assistant manager David Kerslake and first-team coach Joe McBride oversaw the New Year's Day game against Arsenal. After the 2-0 defeat, Kerslake commented on the team's performance and the possibility of a new manager improving the squad. He also stated that he and the staff would continue to work until told otherwise. Malky Mackay, whom Solskjaer was poised to replace, was seen at Celtic Park ahead of Celtic's match against Partick Thistle. Mackay was greeted warmly, seemingly providing a distraction from the circumstances of his departure from Cardiff.

article_content: Reports suggest that Gordon Brown's emails might have been compromised by private investigators linked to British newspapers during his tenure as a top finance official. The Independent newspaper broke this news on Monday. London's Metropolitan Police initiated an investigation in June concerning potential computer hacking activities possibly connected to newspapers. This followed separate investigations into phone hacking and police bribery that began earlier in the year. Authorities have neither confirmed nor denied the possibility that Gordon Brown's communications were targeted when he served as chancellor under Tony Blair. Gordon Brown's representatives have not yet provided comments to CNN regarding these allegations. However, another former high-ranking government official stated that police had contacted him about potential hacking targeting both his official and personal computers. Peter Hain, who previously served as Northern Ireland secretary and has been a long-standing figure within the Labour Party, mentioned that police questioned him about potential hacking incidents occurring between 2005 and 2007. Much of the controversy surrounding phone hacking revolves around the now-defunct News of the World, a popular Sunday tabloid. James Murdoch, its proprietor, closed the newspaper in July due to the escalating scandal. News International, the parent company of the former News of the World, has not issued any statement regarding the Independent's report. The Independent has not disclosed which newspaper allegedly hired the private detectives responsible for targeting government ministers. Operation Tuleta is the name given to the ongoing computer hacking investigation. A 52-year-old man was arrested in Milton Keynes on November 24 as part of this investigation and was later released on bail until March, according to police. Sixteen individuals have been arrested in connection with Operation Weeting, the phone-hacking probe, and eight have been arrested in Operation Elvedon, the bribery investigation. Two of the individuals arrested in the bribery probe were also arrested in the phone-hacking investigation. The phone-hacking saga, initially concerning a few well-known personalities like celebrities, journalists, and politicians, gained international attention last summer when it was revealed that News of the World employees had illegally accessed the messages of a missing teenager who was later found to have been murdered. Former News of the World editors Rebekah Brooks and Andy Coulson have both been arrested and subsequently released on bail. Prime Minister David Cameron faced criticism for hiring Coulson after his resignation due to subordinates pleading guilty to phone hacking. Coulson asserts that he was unaware of any illegal activities. The government has established an independent inquiry to run concurrently with the police investigations. Additionally, parliament's media committee has conducted hearings with witnesses, including News Corporation chairman Rupert Murdoch. His son, James, has been summoned twice as lawmakers attempt to ascertain his knowledge of the phone hacking. Police reports indicate that notebooks belonging to a private investigator central to the scandal contain the names of approximately 5,800 potential victims. According to the Independent, police have seized 20 computers as part of the email hacking investigation. They suggest that the number of computer hacking victims could potentially match the number of phone hacking victims, although the source of this information is not identified.

Myndighederne har hverken bekræftet eller afkræftet muligheden for, at Gordon Browns kommunikation blev målrettet, da han var kansler under Tony Blair. To af de personer, der blev arresteret i bestikkelsesundersøgelsen, blev også arresteret i telefonhacking-undersøgelsen. Tidligere News of the World-redaktører Rebekah Brooks og Andy Coulson er begge blevet arresteret og efterfølgende løsladt mod kaution. Premierminister David Cameron blev kritiseret for at ansætte Coulson efter hans opsigelse, fordi underordnede erklærede sig skyldige i telefonhacking. Coulson hævder, at han ikke var klar over nogen ulovlige aktiviteter. Regeringen har nedsat en uafhængig undersøgelse, der skal køre sideløbende med politiets undersøgelser. Derudover har parlamentets medieudvalg afholdt høringer med vidner, herunder News Corporation-formand Rupert Murdoch. Hans søn, James, er blevet indkaldt to gange, da lovgivere forsøger at fastslå hans viden om telefonhacking. Politiets rapporter indikerer, at notesbøger, der tilhører en privat efterforsker, der er central for skandalen, indeholder navnene på ca. 5.800 potentielle ofre. Ifølge The Independent har politiet beslaglagt 20 computere som en del af e-mail-hackingundersøgelsen. De antyder, at antallet af computerhacking-ofre potentielt kan matche antallet af telefonhacking-ofre, selvom kilden til disse oplysninger ikke er identificeret.

article_content: WHSmith is set to sell a range of eReaders as it aims to counteract the shift away from traditional books. The retailer has signed an agreement to stock two eReaders manufactured by Canadian tech company Kobo, with prices starting at £89. This deal will grant users access to the UK's largest eBook catalogue, featuring over 2.2 million titles, including one million free books. The rise in popularity of devices like Kindle and iPad presents a significant challenge to conventional book sales, which have decreased by approximately 4 percent at WHSmith compared to last year. Kobo's eReader, available in WHSmith stores starting next week, with prices starting at £89, provides access to 2.2 million books and includes a touchscreen Wi-Fi reader in the UK.  Company executives have apparently concluded that entering the virtual book market is the only way to address the threat posed by eBooks. Chief executive Kate Swann stated that this move would complement the retailer's existing physical book sales, rather than simply encouraging customers to switch formats. She added, 'If e-books prove successful, they will incrementally benefit us, given that our physical book customer base tends to consist of lighter book readers.' The Kobo eReader, priced at £89, matches the price of the latest basic Kindle. It weighs 221g and can store up to 10,000 eBooks. A touchscreen version is available for £109.99. The eReaders will be available in WHSmith's 750 stores. British book chain Waterstones has also announced plans to launch its own eBook reader. Books can be transferred between devices, such as smartphones and tablets. Despite the decline in book sales, WHSmith reported a 4 percent increase in profits, reaching £93 million for the year ending August 31. The eBook launch is part of a broader restructuring at the chain, following a strategy of eliminating products with low profit margins, such as CDs and DVDs, to concentrate on core areas like news, magazines, books, and stationery—a move that affected sales but improved profits. Kobo currently has five million customers worldwide and is the largest eBook company in both Canada and Australia. Profits from stores located at airports and train stations increased by eight percent to a record £57 million, although like-for-like sales decreased as passenger numbers were affected by the challenging economic conditions. In the United States, retailers such as Barnes & Noble already sell successful eBook readers. British book chain Waterstone's recently announced its intentions to launch its own eBook reader. article_content: In Michigan, a statutory rape case against Joseph Tarnopolski, age 18, has been dismissed following the suicide of the 14-year-old girl involved, as confirmed by the Wayne County prosecutor's office. Maria Miller, representing the prosecutor's office, stated that the girl's anticipated testimony was crucial evidence. She expressed condolences to the bereaved family, calling it a heartbreaking situation. Samantha Kelly's mother, June Justice, expressed her sorrow and disappointment on Wednesday after Joseph Tarnopolski was released. According to WDIV, a CNN affiliate, June Justice communicated her deep pain. Miller explained that Samantha Kelly's death removed key testimonial evidence needed for a possible conviction and prevented the defendant from being cross-examined. Her body was found by her 12-year-old brother in her bedroom after she hanged herself, as reported by Huron Township Detective Scott Carey. Tarnopolski admitted to the sexual contact but claimed it was consensual. He was charged with third-degree criminal sexual conduct. Tarnopolski told WDIV that the acts were mutual. He blamed the girl's parents, saying they exaggerated the encounter, which he denies. Huron Township police indicated the sexual encounter was consensual, but the alleged victim was under the age of consent. Michigan law requires more than just the defendant's admission to prove a case, despite Tarnopolski's acknowledgment. The girl's mother, in tears, stated that she was separated and informed about the decision prior to the dismissal. She criticised the system. News of Samantha Kelly's death shocked the Wayne County suburb of Detroit. A neighbor named Amy Tyree said that it tears the community up when a young child dies.

Maria Miller, der repræsenterer anklagemyndigheden, udtalte, at pigens forventede vidneudsagn var afgørende som bevis. Hun udtrykte kondolencer til den efterladte familie og kaldte det en hjerteskærende situation. Miller forklarede, at Samantha Kellys død betød, at centrale vidneudsagn, der var nødvendige for en mulig domfældelse, ikke kunne fremlægges, og at den tiltalte ikke kunne krydsforhøres. Hendes lig blev fundet af hendes 12-årige bror i hendes soveværelse, efter at hun havde begået selvmord ved hængning, som rapporteret af Huron Township Detective Scott Carey. Tarnopolski indrømmede den seksuelle kontakt, men hævdede, at den var samtykkebaseret. Han blev anklaget for seksuelt overgreb af tredje grad. Tarnopolski fortalte WDIV, at handlingerne var gensidige. Han gav pigens forældre skylden og sagde, at de overdrev hændelsen, hvilket han benægter. Huron Township-politiet indikerede, at den seksuelle kontakt var samtykkebaseret, men det påståede offer var under den seksuelle lavalder. Michigan-loven kræver mere end blot den tiltaltes indrømmelse for at bevise en sag, uanset Tarnopolskis erkendelse. Pigens mor sagde i tårer, at hun var blevet ført til side og informeret om beslutningen, før sagen blev afvist. Hun kritiserede systemet. Nyheden om Samantha Kellys død chokerede forstaden til Detroit i Wayne County. En nabo ved navn Amy Tyree sagde, at det flår samfundet op, når et ungt barn dør.

article_content: By Associated Press Published: 12:32 EST, March 12, 2014 | Updated: 04:20 EST, March 13, 2014 A Wisconsin town dealing with frozen waterways and clogged drains caused by melted snow tried an unconventional approach: blowing up a creek. Officials in the Town of Onalaska hired a blasting company to place several hundred sticks of plastic explosives in the frozen Sand Lake Coulee Creek and detonate them. Officials turned to explosives after a downpour on February 23 caused water to run on top of the ice and around a dike protecting about a dozen homes. When heavy machinery failed to clear the frozen Sand Lake Coulee Creek, Onalaska officials opted for explosives. Rolly Bogert, Chairman of the Town of Onalaska, said the board sought permits from lawmakers and the Department of Natural Resources to break up the ice. 'That fractured the ice, and the explosions launched the ice straight up in the air before it came back down. There is no debris outside of the creek bed,' he told news8000.com. Following the blast, crews removed the remaining ice and created a channel for the water to flow. No homes in the area sustained damage from the blast. Jerry McManigle said that in his 50 years of experience, he's detonated barns, foundations, and beaver dams, but never a creek. Water now flows freely through Sand Lake Coulee Creek in Onalaska, Wisconsin, after crews used explosives to help clear up to five feet of ice. Crews removed the remaining ice and created a channel for the water after the blast.

article_content: Following the University of Kentucky Wildcats' advancement to the NCAA championship, exuberant students engaged in destructive celebrations, setting fire to vehicles and furniture. Coach John Calipari recognized the intense devotion of the fanbase but voiced his disapproval of certain behaviors. Calipari told reporters that the program is deeply intertwined with the state of Kentucky, acknowledging that their enthusiasm sometimes exceeds acceptable boundaries. The Wildcats, who held the top seed, secured a 69-61 victory against their in-state rivals, Louisville, during a semifinal game of the NCAA tournament, commonly known as March Madness. This triumph incited scores of Wildcat supporters to leave establishments and residences in Lexington, the university's city, and swarm the streets, expressing their joy through raised fists and loud cheers. Local law enforcement officials observed the festivities, including students celebrating around burning cars and couches, according to police Lieutenant Mark Brand. CNN affiliate WLEX broadcasted footage depicting flames reaching high into the night sky as fire trucks struggled to navigate the crowded streets. Reports from the University of Kentucky's Twitter account indicated several criminal events and the temporary shutdown of multiple roadways. Brand, representing Lexington police, noted that authorities didn't fully regain control of State Street until nearly 1 a.m., approximately four hours after the game concluded. Although some students were apprehended, the precise number of arrests was not disclosed by the police. Brand mentioned that one individual sustained a minor injury, specifically a scraped knee. Calipari defended the Kentucky fanbase during a press conference held in New Orleans, where his team is preparing to compete against the University of Kansas in the championship game on Monday night. Bookmakers have positioned the Wildcats, who entered the tournament as the nation's top-ranked team, as favorites in the upcoming contest. The coach emphasized that while Kentucky fans are passionate about their team and celebrate victories, they would never disrespect their opponents. Calipari asserted that their fans are remarkably well-mannered, highlighting that they would never engage in behaviors such as rushing the court after a significant win or acting aggressively towards opposing teams.

article_content: As Facebook prepared for its initial public offering (IPO), estimated at $79.3 billion, the real estate market in Palo Alto experienced a noticeable surge. This increase in property values may not be welcomed by prospective homebuyers in the area. With the anticipation of new millionaires emerging from Facebook's stock launch, housing prices in Palo Alto, already among the highest nationwide, are projected to climb further. Despite a general downturn in housing sales across the country, Palo Alto and its surrounding areas have remained a prominent hotspot, according to the New York Times. The number of homes available for purchase has also decreased substantially, by as much as 57%. Mark Zuckerberg, who became the world’s youngest billionaire three years prior, invested in Palo Alto's real estate by purchasing a $7 million, five-bedroom house with his girlfriend, Priscilla Chan. This property is conveniently located a ten-minute drive from Facebook's headquarters in Menlo Park. Before this purchase, Zuckerberg resided in a more typical home. Ken DeLeon, a Silicon Valley real estate agent, shared with the Times an instance where a Facebook employee upgraded from a 1,000-square-foot house to an 8,000-square-foot property. DeLeon humorously inquired if the employee had ‘won the lottery.’ This trend appears to extend beyond just one or two Facebook employees. According to Coldwell Banker, Silicon Valley claimed eight of the twenty most expensive real estate locations in the country in 2011. DeLeon suggests that current and future homeowners have several choices leading up to the IPO. They can either remain in their homes and hope for increased property values or participate in house-flipping—buying, renovating, and reselling properties for profit. Data from BrokerMetrics indicates that the median home price in Palo Alto rose by 11% last year, while housing inventory dropped by 57%. Listings on Trulia.com reveal that even modest homes are priced in the millions. National Association of Realtors Chief Economist Lawrence Yun stated that the housing market showed signs of recovery in 2012. Yun noted that increasing sales were reducing inventory, thus creating balanced conditions nationwide, which could lead to rising home prices in more areas. However, Fortune suggests that if Facebook's IPO underperforms, the region's housing market could decline, potentially bringing a housing downturn to Silicon Valley. Additionally, 'the Facebook effect' may be driving private sales, where homeowners avoid public listings to maintain privacy and exclusivity.

Med forventningen om, at nye millionærer vil opstå som følge af Facebooks børsnotering, forventes boligpriserne i Palo Alto, som allerede er blandt de højeste i landet, at stige yderligere. På trods af en generel nedgang i boligsalget i resten af landet, er Palo Alto og de omkringliggende områder forblevet et attraktivt område, ifølge New York Times. Antallet af boliger til salg er også faldet markant, med op til 57%. Mark Zuckerberg, der blev verdens yngste milliardær tre år tidligere, investerede i ejendomme i Palo Alto ved at købe et hus med fem soveværelser til 7 millioner dollars sammen med sin kæreste, Priscilla Chan. Denne ejendom er belejligt placeret ti minutters kørsel fra Facebooks hovedkvarter i Menlo Park. Før dette køb boede Zuckerberg i et mere beskedent hjem. Ken DeLeon, en ejendomsmægler i Silicon Valley, fortalte til New York Times om en Facebook-medarbejder, der opgraderede fra et hus på 1.000 kvadratfod til en ejendom på 8.000 kvadratfod. De kan enten blive i deres hjem og håbe på, at ejendomsværdien stiger, eller de kan kaste sig over 'house flipping' - at købe, renovere og sælge ejendomme med fortjeneste. Fortune antyder dog, at hvis Facebooks børsnotering skuffer, kan boligmarkedet i området falde, hvilket potentielt kan bringe en boligkrise til Silicon Valley. Derudover kan 'Facebook-effekten' føre til flere private salg, hvor boligejere undgår offentlige annoncer for at beskytte deres privatliv og eksklusivitet.

article_content: A significant fire in California claimed one life and left six people injured, as flames raged from Wednesday night into the early hours of Thursday. The four-alarm fire erupted around 6:50 p.m. on Wednesday in a large building located in San Francisco's Mission District, according to ABC7 News. Local Fire Chief Joanne Hayes White informed Mission Local that there was one confirmed fatality, an adult male, and six individuals are currently hospitalized receiving treatment for smoke inhalation and burn injuries. Details surrounding the man's death have not been disclosed. The fire is believed to have originated in the attic of the building near 22nd and Mission streets and quickly spread. Flames rapidly engulfed the building's roof and top floor, according to the San Jose Mercury News. By 7:33 p.m., the second floor of the three-story structure was ablaze as numerous firefighters battled the intense flames on the building's roof. An official reported that firefighters conducted at least 11 rescues by approximately 11 p.m., with several individuals being rescued from fire escapes and stairwells where they had sought safety from the fire. According to Mission Local, portions of the building began to collapse as firefighters sprayed water to extinguish the blaze. Hayes White stated that firefighters had rescued at least 11 individuals by around 11 p.m., including some from fire escapes and others from stairwells where they had sought refuge. Arson investigators arrived at the scene as the fire continued to burn and will be conducting an inquiry into its cause. Mission Local reports that at least 40 people have been displaced as a result of the massive fire, and the Red Cross has established a temporary assistance center for the affected individuals at the City College of San Francisco's Mission Campus. The building housed restaurants and shops on the ground floor, offices on the second floor, and apartments on the third floor. The fire remained uncontrolled as of 1:30 a.m. on Thursday. Mission Local further reports that at least 40 individuals are displaced due to the extensive fire, and the Red Cross has created a temporary unit for victims at City College of San Francisco's Mission Campus.

article_content: By Jill Reilly PUBLISHED: 07:10 EST, July 16, 2013 UPDATED: 12:16 EST, July 16, 2013 Phil Spector's daughter reveals the toll of prison life on her father. Spector, 73, is serving 19 years to life for the 2003 murder of actress Lana Clarkson. Nicole Audrey Spector, 30, said each time she sees her 'pop', he looks 'thinner, wispier'. Nicole Audrey Spector, 30, has spoken about her father's life in jail. Before the killing: Nicole poses with her father in 2000, three years before he shot actress Lana Clarkson. The music producer, who worked with The Beatles, is currently housed in California State Prison, Corcoran. In 2009, he was found guilty of shooting the 40-year-old actress in the mouth in the foyer of his California mansion. Nicole is one of Spector's five children; she was born when the musician was with his then-girlfriend Janis Zavala. Her twin brother, Philip Jr., died of leukaemia at age ten. Guilty: In 2009, Spector was found guilty of shooting the 40-year-old actress in the mouth in the foyer of his sprawling California mansion. Grim: The California mansion where Spector shot the actress. Evidence: The Colt revolver found near Clarkson's body is seen in an evidence photo from the trial. Spector was famous for his Wall of Sound production technique, which earned him hits including The Beatles' 'Let It Be'. He also co-wrote 'You've Lost That Lovin' Feelin'' for The Righteous Brothers and produced records for The Ramones. Nicole, now a writer, said in an article for The Times that her father is innocent: 'My father, who I love, didn’t kill anyone. Neither of us is supposed to be here.' She said her visits have become less frequent because she doesn't have a home in California. Changing image: Spector in court in 2005, left, and with his third wife Rachelle Short in 2007. Sporadic: Over the years, Spector has dramatically altered his appearance. 'The last time I visited was nine months ago, a fact that makes me anxious and ashamed. I feel I should be there every weekend, but I don’t have a home in California anymore. I used to stay in my old room in my father’s house, which he still has, but his wife won’t allow it, and I’m not up for the fight anymore.' She refers to Spector's third wife, Rachelle Short, a model and actress around 40 years his junior. The couple met at a Hollywood restaurant in 2003, shortly after his arrest for the shooting of Lana Clarkson. Rachelle became Spector's assistant and was running his business by the time they married in 2006 in the foyer of his mansion, where Clarkson was found dead. Spector's initial trial in 2007 for Lana Clarkson's murder ended in a deadlocked jury. Clarkson died from a gunshot wound to the head. But a second jury in 2009 found him guilty of second-degree murder and sentenced him to 19 years in prison. Throughout both hearings, Spector's defense team claimed that Clarkson killed herself due to her failing film career. Spector met the actress, 40, at a Hollywood nightclub where she worked as a hostess and invited her to his Alhambra mansion. While Spector maintained his innocence, he chose not to testify. His chauffeur, Adriano de Souza, testified that he saw Spector clutching a pistol after Clarkson was shot, saying: 'I think I just killed somebody.' Spector, obsessed with guns, liked to boast about pulling a pistol on John Lennon in a recording studio. Ultimately, his violent past caught up with him. He worked with stars like The Beatles, Tina Turner, The Ronettes, and The Righteous Brothers and revolutionized pop production in the 1960s. Wall of sound: Spector with George Harrison and The Ronettes, including his first wife Veronica Bennett. Women testified about Spector's drunken attacks, often involving guns. They described him as an out-of-control maniac, drunk on his reputation and convinced he was above the law. Threatened and terrorized by Spector, his victims - who were either dating him or longtime friends - never called police. Only when Clarkson's body was found in a pool of blood in the early hours of February 3, 2003 - with Spector standing over her with a gun - did his previous victims come forward. They told the court similar stories of Spector flying into a rage after drinking too much and threatening them with guns when they tried to leave.

article_content: In a recent operation, Mexican military forces liberated 165 individuals, largely Central American citizens including minors and expectant mothers, from a kidnapping ordeal in northeastern Mexico. These individuals were held captive approximately one mile from the United States border, according to government reports released Thursday. The rescued group, predominantly composed of people from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, were seeking entry into the United States via the turbulent northern region of Tamaulipas. They were seized in separate incidents close to the border over a period of two to three weeks and confined to a residence within the Gustavo Diaz Ordaz municipality. Video footage is available. Among those rescued was also a citizen of India. According to Eduardo Sanchez, a government security spokesperson, the evidence suggests that human traffickers initially contacted these migrants. However, instead of facilitating their journey to the border, these criminals reportedly handed them over to criminal organizations. Sanchez added that the migrants were discovered held against their will by an armed person in unsanitary, overcrowded, and perilous circumstances. The rescue operation took place on Tuesday. Tamaulipas has been grappling with a surge in kidnappings and violence in recent years, serving as a long-standing battleground for rival drug cartels. The migrants, originating mainly from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, aspired to enter the U.S. through this northern state known for its instability. The rescued individuals included children and pregnant women, all victims of a kidnapping orchestrated by a gunman in northeastern Mexico, held captive within a mile of the American border. In 2010, Mexican Marines unearthed 72 bodies at a ranch near the border within the same state, believed to be those of migrant workers. This discovery marked the most significant single find during a violent drug conflict that has claimed approximately 75,000 lives since 2006. In recent times, Mexican cartels have extended their operations into human smuggling, abducting migrants and either demanding extortion money or coercing them into transporting drugs across the border.

article_content: Ally McCoist asserted that Rangers' precarious financial state doesn't shield him from potential dismissal. However, the Ibrox manager remains optimistic that he can weather the current criticism and achieve his objective of leading the club back to the top tier of Scottish football. McCoist has faced considerable criticism following Monday evening’s disappointing 3-1 home defeat to Hibernian, which left Rangers trailing Hearts by six points. Ally McCoist acknowledges that no manager is entirely immune to being sacked. Some fans have speculated whether the compensation package related to his £400,000 annual salary makes his dismissal too costly for the board to contemplate. The Ibrox side had to launch a short-term £3.13 million share issue last month and could encounter another cash shortfall before the year concludes. But McCoist stated: ‘I don’t believe anyone is invulnerable. I certainly wouldn’t claim to be. While I’m still under scrutiny, nobody is impervious.’ When asked if suggestions that he was retained solely for financial reasons were offensive, McCoist responded: ‘I don’t find that insulting at all. I don’t necessarily agree with it. I don’t think there has ever been a manager who couldn’t be dismissed.’ Sections of the Ibrox supporters jeered their team after the surprising 3-1 home loss to Hibernian. ‘So, I don’t dwell on that at all, and it doesn’t bother me that people have said it. I’m far too preoccupied with focusing on the positives and moving forward.’ Former players and commentators have heavily criticized McCoist’s leadership this week, with former Hearts midfielder Michael Stewart accusing him of inadequate coaching. ‘I’m not going to pretend that it’s enjoyable when you’re being criticized,’ said the 52-year-old, who declined to comment on specific remarks. ‘Of course, it isn’t. But I accept that it’s part of the job. If Walter Smith, despite achieving Nine-In-A-Row and reaching the UEFA Cup final, still faced criticism, then it’s fair to say we’ll also receive our share. I simply want to accomplish the task at hand.’ The Hibs defeat followed an earlier victory for Hearts at Ibrox. McCoist doesn’t see any reason to panic as he takes his team to Livingston this afternoon. ‘I accept that criticism will follow the two defeats,’ he said. ‘But it’s my responsibility to address that. We’re less than a fifth of the way through the season. There’s still a long way to go.’ ‘It’s important not to overreact after good performances, and I won’t be overly upset after a 3-1 defeat at home to Hibs. I made sure to check, and in 2010, we had a team with nine players who played in the UEFA Cup final that lost 3-0 to Hibs at home. Three years before that, Ivan Sproule scored a hat-trick for Hibs in another 3-0 loss.’ ‘Now, that’s not an excuse. We were beaten 3-1; we had a poor 20 minutes, and we need to rectify that. But it’s not unprecedented. Rangers will be without Bilel Mohsni this weekend after he was suspended for reacting violently to Liam Fontaine.’ ‘Nothing that’s happened this season has shocked us. We knew from the outset that it was a step up.’ The Championship play-offs would provide an alternative route if Rangers can’t close the gap on Hearts. ‘Getting out of the division is the priority,’ McCoist added. ‘We’ll take any opportunity to get out of this division because it’s crucial for the club to return to the top flight as soon as possible.’

På spørgsmålet om, hvorvidt antydninger om, at han udelukkende blev beholdt af økonomiske årsager, var stødende, svarede McCoist: 'Jeg finder det slet ikke fornærmende. Hvis Walter Smith, på trods af at have opnået Nine-In-A-Row og nået UEFA Cup-finalen, stadig stod over for kritik, så er det fair at sige, at vi også vil få vores del. Jeg vil simpelthen bare udføre opgaven.' Hibs-nederlaget fulgte efter en tidligere sejr til Hearts på Ibrox. McCoist ser ingen grund til panik, når han tager sit hold til Livingston i eftermiddag. 'Jeg accepterer, at kritik vil følge de to nederlag,' sagde han. 'Men det er mit ansvar at adressere det. Vi er mindre end en femtedel inde i sæsonen. Der er stadig lang vej igen.' 'Det er vigtigt ikke at overreagere efter gode præstationer, og jeg vil ikke være alt for ked af det efter et 3-1 nederlag hjemme til Hibs. Jeg sørgede for at tjekke, og i 2010 havde vi et hold med ni spillere, der spillede i UEFA Cup-finalen, som tabte 3-0 til Hibs hjemme. Tre år før det scorede Ivan Sproule et hattrick for Hibs i endnu et 3-0-tab.' 'Nu er det ikke en undskyldning. Vi blev slået 3-1; vi havde 20 dårlige minutter, og det skal vi rette op på. Men det er ikke uden fortilfælde. Rangers må undvære Bilel Mohsni i denne weekend, efter at han blev suspenderet for voldelig adfærd mod Liam Fontaine.' 'Intet af det, der er sket i denne sæson, har chokeret os. Vi vidste fra starten, at det var et trin opad.' Championship-playoffkampene vil være en alternativ vej, hvis Rangers ikke kan indhente Hearts. 'At komme ud af divisionen er førsteprioriteten,' tilføjede McCoist. 'Vi vil gribe enhver mulighed for at komme ud af denne division, fordi det er afgørende for klubben at vende tilbage til den bedste række hurtigst muligt.'
