article_content: Thai authorities are looking for more individuals possibly tied to the Bangkok bombings that occurred last week, as they continue to investigate a complex case involving accusations between Israel and Iran. An arrest warrant has been issued by a court for Norouzi Shayan Ali Akbar, a 57-year-old Iranian, on charges related to possessing and assembling explosives. This is the fifth warrant issued in the probe. According to Gen. Pansiri Prapawat, the deputy national police chief leading the investigation, another warrant may be requested for a sixth, as-yet-unidentified suspect, pending further evidence. Investigators have shifted their focus away from Nikkhahfard Javad, whom they previously intended to seek a warrant for. The Bangkok explosions followed a bombing in New Delhi targeting an Israeli Embassy vehicle, which injured several individuals. Additionally, a device was discovered on an embassy vehicle in Tbilisi, Georgia, and safely detonated. The Thai National Security Council suggests a connection between the Bangkok bombings and those in India and Georgia, noting similarities in the explosives used. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directly accused Iran of orchestrating the attacks, a claim that Iran has refuted, asserting that Israel often stages such events. Indian police have been silent regarding their investigation into the New Delhi bombing. P.N. Aggarwal, head of the investigating police unit, declined to comment on potential leads. As of yet, Indian authorities have not identified any Iranian suspects. Thai officials report that three Iranian suspects are in custody: Saeid Moradi, 28, who lost his legs in an explosion involving his own bomb; Mohammad Khazaei, 42, apprehended at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport while attempting to fly to Malaysia; and Masoud Sedaghatzadeh, 31, detained in Kuala Lumpur by Malaysian authorities, with Thailand seeking his extradition. All three are charged with jointly assembling explosives, possessing them without permits, and causing injury through an explosion. Moradi also faces charges for attempted murder of state officials and other individuals. Rohani Leila, a fourth Iranian suspect, remains at large. She is believed to have rented the property where the initial explosion occurred. Khazaei, wearing a bulletproof vest and handcuffs, was taken by police to various locations in Bangkok, including the bomb sites, as part of the investigation. He was observed indicating specific areas to detectives at a busy train station for approximately 20 minutes. CNN's Harmeet Singh and Anna Coren contributed to this report.
translated_content: De thailandske myndigheder leder efter flere personer, der muligvis er forbundet med bombeangrebene i Bangkok i sidste uge, mens de fortsætter med at undersøge en kompleks sag, der involverer beskyldninger mellem Israel og Iran. En arrestordre er udstedt af en domstol for Norouzi Shayan Ali Akbar, en 57-årig iraner, for anklager relateret til besiddelse og samling af sprængstoffer. Dette er den femte arrestordre, der er udstedt i efterforskningen. Ifølge general Pansiri Prapawat, vicechef for det nationale politi og leder af efterforskningen, kan der blive anmodet om endnu en arrestordre for en sjette, endnu ikke identificeret mistænkt, afhængigt af yderligere beviser. Efterforskerne har flyttet deres fokus væk fra Nikkhahfard Javad, som de tidligere havde til hensigt at søge en arrestordre på. Eksplosionerne i Bangkok fulgte et bombeangreb i New Delhi rettet mod en israelsk ambassadebil, hvor flere personer blev såret. Derudover blev en enhed opdaget i en ambassadebil i Tbilisi, Georgien, og den blev uskadeliggjort ved kontrolleret sprængning. Det thailandske nationale sikkerhedsråd antyder en forbindelse mellem bombeangrebene i Bangkok og dem i Indien og Georgien, og bemærker ligheder i de anvendte sprængstoffer. Israels premierminister Benjamin Netanyahu har direkte beskyldt Iran for at stå bag angrebene, en påstand som Iran har afvist og hævder, at Israel ofte selv iscenesætter sådanne terrorhandlinger. Det indiske politi har været tavse omkring deres efterforskning af bombeangrebet i New Delhi. P.N. Aggarwal, leder af den efterforskende politienhed, afviste at kommentere potentielle spor. Indtil videre har de indiske myndigheder ikke identificeret nogen iranske mistænkte. Thailandske embedsmænd rapporterer, at tre iranske mistænkte er i varetægt: Saeid Moradi, 28, som mistede sine ben i en eksplosion med sin egen bombe; Mohammad Khazaei, 42, anholdt i Bangkoks Suvarnabhumi Lufthavn, mens han forsøgte at flyve til Malaysia; og Masoud Sedaghatzadeh, 31, tilbageholdt i Kuala Lumpur af malaysiske myndigheder, hvor Thailand søger hans udlevering. Alle tre er anklaget for i forening at have samlet sprængstoffer, besiddet dem uden tilladelse og forårsaget skade gennem en eksplosion. Moradi er også anklaget for forsøg på drab på statslige embedsmænd og andre personer. Rohani Leila, en fjerde iransk mistænkt, er fortsat på fri fod. Hun menes at have lejet den ejendom, hvor den første eksplosion fandt sted. Khazaei, iført en skudsikker vest og håndjern, blev ført af politiet til forskellige steder i Bangkok, herunder gerningsstederne for bombeangrebene, som en del af efterforskningen. Han blev observeret, da han pegede på specifikke områder for efterforskere på en travl togstation i ca. 20 minutter. CNN's Harmeet Singh og Anna Coren bidrog til denne rapport.

article_content: In Puerto Rico, thousands protested government budget cuts in downtown San Juan on Thursday, halting commercial activities. These cuts could lead to roughly 13,000 job losses. According to Gov. Luis Fortuño's office, the island's economic struggles began in 2005. A demonstrator's sign read, 'More employees, zero fired.' The strike lasted one day, beginning at dawn and culminating with a rally at Plaza las Americas at noon. Rally organizers estimated 100,000 attendees, with additional thousands absent from work. Union leader Federico Torres Montalvo claimed 200,000 attended the rally, while Secretary of State Kenneth McClintock estimated closer to 15,000. There was no independent confirmation of the turnout. After the rally, confrontations between police and students blocking a highway subsided late Thursday afternoon. Some students remained on the blocked highway, according to primerahora.com. Police increased their presence, and students burned a tire. No violence or arrests were reported. Gov. Luis Fortuño commented that such actions in Washington D.C. would lead to arrests. He urged looking forward, instead of backward. Victor Villalba, president of the Puerto Rican Federation of Workers, praised the turnout and criticized government privatization plans. He stated strong opposition to privatizing government businesses. Aida Diaz, the teacher's union president, also applauded the rally's participation, emphasizing public education's importance. University students, teachers, and religious leaders participated in the strike. Methodist Bishop Juan Vera negotiated with protesting students. Bishop Vera described the palpable energy of the people. Six protesters received medical attention for heat-related issues, per primerahora. One woman was transported by ambulance. Gov. Fortuño affirmed the right to protest peacefully in an interview with WAPA TV. He emphasized maintaining respect and order during demonstrations. News reports indicated no significant incidents at protest sites. Minor altercations occurred between University of Puerto Rico students and police at the mall before the rally, with no arrests. article_content: A remarkable collection of photographs, captured in China and Japan, that provided the Western world with some of its earliest views of the Far East is set to be auctioned. In particular, an image showing Chinese corpses at North Fort in Peiho in 1860 serves as a stark reminder of the Second Opium War. The North Fort was one of the Taku Forts, strategically positioned defenses in China guarding the mouth of the Peiho River. The fort, located near modern-day Tianjin, was breached on August 20, 1860, and its garrison surrendered after a fierce battle. Renowned photographer Felice Beato took these pictures while accompanying the British Army. The battlements and cannons are depicted surrounded by Chinese corpses, following the fort's capture by English and French forces. The Opium Wars represented the culmination of trade disputes between China and the British Empire concerning Chinese efforts to restrict British opium trafficking. China was defeated in both the First Opium War (1839-1842) and the Second Opium War (1856-1860). Felice Beato travelled with the British Army during the Indian Rebellion and the Second Opium War in China. Beato also captured the Imperial Summer Palace in Beijing before its destruction by fire in 1860. This collection includes images of Gan Kiro, Yokohama, and other scenes illustrating life in the Far East at the time. The photographs, taken by Felice Beato, who travelled with the British Army, include views of Yokohama and other locations. Approximately 68 prints made from the original negatives were compiled into an album that Beato sold to Captain Roderick Dew. This album has remained in the Dew family for 150 years, serving as a record of the Captain's service in China and Japan. Beato's images also include a panoramic view of Hong Kong harbor, the Forbidden City in Peking, a pagoda, and scenes of slain Chinese soldiers at a fort. Around 68 prints from the negatives were made into an album sold to Captain Roderick Dew. Beato's photography studio in Yokohama, Japan, was destroyed by fire shortly after, further enhancing the historical value of these prints. The album has remained in the Dew family for the last 150 years, serving as a record of his service in China and Japan. The collection includes a portrait of representatives from the US, England, and France, including Captain Roderick Dew. The photographs are being auctioned at Lawrences Auctioneers of Crewkerne, Somerset, and are expected to fetch up to £70,000. The auctioneers describe the photo album as 'one of the most extensive and historically significant to appear on the market in many years'. The album contains 68 individual prints and is expected to fetch up to £70,000 on January 31. Beato's images also encompass a panoramic view of Hong Kong harbor and the Forbidden City in Peking. Robert Ansell, of Lawrences, stated, 'This album is one of the most extensive and historically significant to appear on the market in many years.' 'It is also one of the earliest recorded from the studio of Felice Beato in Yokohama, widely regarded as an important pioneer of photography in the Far East.' 'The album contains 68 individual prints that are amongst the earliest photographs that record both China and Japan.' The Tycoons Palace in Yedo is featured in a folding two-print panorama photograph taken by Felice Beato. Beato's photography studio in Yokohama, Japan, was destroyed by fire shortly after, further enhancing the historical value of this album. The folding panoramas of views provided many in the Western world with an initial glimpse into the Far East. The collection also features 11 folding panoramic views and a portrait by Felice Beato of Captain Dew with representatives of American, French, and British forces. Captain Dew (1823-1869) played a significant role in the attack on the Taku Forts during the Second Opium War in 1859. As Commander of HMS Nimrod, Captain Dew described the attack in a personal letter: 'We had to steam some distance before our guns would bear and then six shells plumped right into the Southern forts and exploded.' 'I saw the poor devils carried out in a fearful state - many naked and quite black… the huge brass guns tumbled about.'

Kina blev besejret i både den Første Opiumskrig (1839-1842) og den Anden Opiumskrig (1856-1860). Felice Beato rejste med den britiske hær under det indiske oprør og den Anden Opiumskrig i Kina. Samlingen indeholder også 11 foldbare panoramaudsigter og et portræt af Felice Beato af kaptajn Dew med repræsentanter for amerikanske, franske og britiske styrker. Som kommandør for HMS Nimrod beskrev kaptajn Dew angrebet i et personligt brev: 'Vi måtte dampe et stykke tid, før vores kanoner kunne bære, og så plaskede seks granater lige ind i de sydlige forter og eksploderede.' article_content: Fitness enthusiasts now have a new must-have gadget. Instead of relying on sports watches, a digital running shirt with advanced features is available. Inventors have developed a digital running shirt that combines the capabilities of an electronic tracking device with added functionalities. The 'D-Shirt', created by French company Cityzen Sciences, was showcased with basketball players. The special fabric includes sensors to record heart rate, GPS location, route, speed, and altitude. The shirt uses a Smart Sensing fabric with integrated micro-sensors to collect data. Information is sent to a small detachable transmitter on the back of the shirt, which transmits data to a smartphone via Bluetooth. The transmitter must be removed before washing the garment. Transmissions are effective within 10 meters of the phone; data is synchronized upon the runner's return if the phone is left behind. Real-time monitoring is possible if the runner or trainer carries the phone. The app stores and analyzes data, displaying the runner’s route and speed. A session summary includes route, time, speed, heart rate, and calories burned. The lightweight, washable garment transmits information to a smartphone app via Bluetooth, allowing progress tracking and performance review. The shirt allows remote monitoring during workouts, appealing to marathon runners. Developers claim the shirt's data can indicate overexertion and potential heart attack risk. Stanislas Vandier, deputy chief executive, stated their aim is to simplify connected living, integrating technology seamlessly into daily routines. 'You never leave home without a shirt. So we are simply turning a T-shirt into a D-shirt.' The D-shirt connects to an app displaying journey duration, distance, heart-rate, calories burned, speed and level of fatigue. Future applications may extend to other garments like shorts and sports bras. The shirt is presented at the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona, with a French launch in September. Cityzen Sciences is negotiating with British retailers for a UK release. The male and female versions of the shirt utilize Smart Sensing fabric with integral micro-sensors, transmitting data to smartphones via Bluetooth. Applications extend to athletes, first responders, and soldiers in extreme conditions. Smart Sensing fabric is 30-40% pricier than standard material, and developers are creating sensors for heat, respiration, and perspiration. Future versions may monitor blood oxygen and glucose levels. Jean-Luc Errant, company chief executive, initiated the D-Shirt concept in 2003 and secured £16 million for its development. Cityzen Sciences, founded in 2008, specializes in smart textiles and collaborates with various companies.

article_content: In Detroit, a tragic incident on Christmas Day led to the death of 16-year-old Bernard Walker. According to police reports and WJBK, Bernard was at a residence in the Petosky-Otsego area when two friends visited, one bringing a loaded handgun. While in the basement, the friends began carelessly handling the weapon. The 19-year-old companion discharged the firearm, hitting Bernard in the head. Bernard was quickly transported to Henry Ford Hospital and placed on life support. Sadly, he passed away on Friday afternoon after life support was withdrawn. A neighbor remembered Bernard as a 'good kid.' His mother, Theresa Culbert, expressed the heartbreak of witnessing her son's final moments, stating, 'Just basically had to watch his brain die.' Police have taken both friends into custody. Jennifer Moreno, spokesperson for the Detroit Police Department, informed Detroit News that the 19-year-old is being held, and they will pursue charges related to Bernard's death. Officer Moreno indicated that the Wayne County Prosecutor’s Office will determine the charges, likely manslaughter or second-degree murder. Friends announced on Twitter that a candlelight vigil would be held on Monday to honor Bernard. Authorities are also investigating whether the handgun was properly registered. At the time of the report, the registration check had not yet been completed.

Mens de var i kælderen, begyndte vennerne skødesløst at håndtere våbnet. Den 19-årige affyrede våbnet og ramte Bernard i hovedet. Bernard blev hurtigt transporteret til Henry Ford Hospital og blev lagt i respirator. Desværre døde han fredag eftermiddag, efter at respiratoren blev fjernet. En nabo huskede Bernard som en 'god dreng'. Hans mor, Theresa Culbert, udtrykte den hjerteskærende oplevelse af at være vidne til sin søns sidste øjeblikke og sagde: 'Jeg var dybest set bare nødt til at se hans hjerne dø.' Politiet har anholdt begge venner. Jennifer Moreno, der er talskvinde for Detroit Police Department, oplyste til Detroit News, at den 19-årige er blevet tilbageholdt, og at de vil rejse tiltale i forbindelse med Bernards død. Betjent Moreno indikerede, at anklagemyndigheden i Wayne County vil afgøre, hvilken tiltale der skal rejses; sandsynligvis uagtsomt manddrab eller drab. Venner annoncerede på Twitter, at der vil blive afholdt en mindehøjtidelighed på mandag for at ære Bernard. Myndighederne undersøger også, hvorvidt pistolen var korrekt registreret. Registreringstjekket var endnu ikke afsluttet på tidspunktet for rapporten.

article_content: A zookeeper is blaming himself for a near-fatal encounter with a crocodile that resulted in the loss of his thumb. He admits to having limited recollection of the traumatic event. Ian Jenkins, the owner of Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo near Childers, Queensland, was attacked by a crocodile during a performance in front of a large audience. The 58-year-old was dragged into the pond by the four-metre crocodile, known as ‘Macca,’ who then initiated a death roll. His colleague, Louise Smith, acted quickly, saving Jenkins' life. ‘I’m relieved but also so annoyed,’ Jenkins told Seven News from his hospital bed. 'You just don’t get yourself into that situation with a crocodile!' He attributed the incident to ‘just a bit of a brain freeze.’ Jenkins is recovering in hospital following the near-death experience. While Jenkins claims responsibility, his colleague Louise Smith agrees that the crocodile is typically very docile. However, the four-metre crocodile 'Macca' was responsible for the attack. Smith maintains she was simply doing her job when she distracted Macca to free Jenkins. Onlookers, including many young children, witnessed the terrifying ordeal and are struggling to process the violent attack. The incident disrupted what was intended as a fun holiday activity for families. Witness Emma Murray Bryant, visibly shaken, recounted Jenkins’ narrow escape to Seven News. ‘He kneeled down and put his hat near his nose, and the croc snapped, and you knew…' Ms. Bryant stated. 'It didn’t look good. Then the croc snapped at him the second time, and that’s when he got him.’ She continues to be haunted by the sickening sound of the two 'snaps' she heard, reliving the moment Macca attacked his keeper. Smith explains that intervening in such situations is part of her job, emphasizing the protocol of having a second handler present during crocodile shows. Jenkins, the owner of Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo, suffered a severed thumb and head injuries when the crocodile grabbed him and pulled him into the water. He was airlifted to hospital in stable condition. Smith used a stick to repeatedly strike the crocodile's head until it released Jenkins. ‘I just tried to distract (the crocodile) to give me and Ian a chance to get out of there,’ she said. Following the attack, Jenkins, 58, was airlifted to Bundaberg Base Hospital with a head injury. He was later transferred to Brisbane Hospital and has undergone several hours of surgery to reconstruct his hand. The incident occurred when Jenkins attempted to attract Macca’s attention with a chicken in his right hand. Macca unexpectedly lunged at his other hand, tearing a section of his left hand down to the wrist. Reportedly, Jenkins apologized to paramedics for 'causing such a fuss'. The 58-year-old reptile park owner was attacked at Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo. His passion for reptiles began in his childhood in Kenya, and he has been a respected member of the Childers community for over 30 years. This is not the first serious injury Jenkins has sustained on the job. Five years prior, he survived an eastern brown snake bite and in 2003, he was bitten by a king brown snake and two black snakes before that. In January 2010, while preparing an eastern brown snake for a show, he was bitten through a bag, resulting in his collapse and loss of consciousness. He received anti-venom treatment and returned to performing soon after. Jenkins has lived in Australia for about 30 years and is very knowledgeable about reptiles. His wife, Barbara Jenkins, emphasizes that he doesn't seek out danger but is motivated by his passion for reptiles and educating others. Jenkins has expressed that his primary concern is his family and the distress caused by his injuries. The park operated as usual the day after the attack, except for the crocodile feeding shows, which are expected to resume once Jenkins recovers. Smith stated that Macca is normally calm and that the aggressive behavior was unusual. However, the incident served as a stark reminder of the inherent dangers. Paramedics responded to the zoo at 12:55 pm local time, according to a Queensland Ambulance Service spokesman. The crocodile attack occurred at Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo and follows a recent increase in crocodile attacks in the Northern Territory.
translated_content: En dyrepasser giver sig selv skylden for et nær-dødeligt møde med en krokodille, der resulterede i tabet af hans tommelfinger. Han indrømmer, at han har begrænsede erindringer om den traumatiske begivenhed. Ian Jenkins, ejeren af Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo nær Childers i Queensland, blev angrebet af en krokodille under en forestilling foran et stort publikum. Den 58-årige mand blev trukket ned i dammen af den fire meter lange krokodille, kendt som 'Macca', som derefter startede en dødsrulle. Hans kollega, Louise Smith, reagerede hurtigt og reddede Jenkins' liv. ‘Jeg er lettet, men også så irriteret,’ fortalte Jenkins til Seven News fra sin hospitalsseng. 'Man skal bare ikke bringe sig selv i sådan en situation med en krokodille!' Han tilskrev hændelsen ‘bare en smule hjernefrysning.’ Jenkins er ved at komme sig på hospitalet efter den nær-dødelige oplevelse. Mens Jenkins selv tager skylden, er hans kollega Louise Smith enig i, at krokodillen typisk er meget rolig. Ikke desto mindre var den fire meter lange krokodille 'Macca' ansvarlig for angrebet. Smith fastholder, at hun blot gjorde sit arbejde, da hun distraherede Macca for at befri Jenkins. Tilskuere, herunder mange små børn, var vidne til den skræmmende oplevelse og kæmper for at bearbejde det voldsomme angreb. Hændelsen forstyrrede det, der var tiltænkt som en sjov ferieaktivitet for familier. Vidnet Emma Murray Bryant, der var synligt rystet, genfortalte Jenkins' snævre flugt til Seven News. ‘Han knælede ned og holdt sin hat tæt på næsen, og krokodillen snappede, og man vidste, hvad der ville ske…’ udtalte Emma Murray Bryant. 'Det så ikke godt ud. Så snappede krokodillen efter ham anden gang, og det var der, den fik fat i ham.’ Hun er fortsat hjemsøgt af den uhyggelige lyd af de to 'snaps', hun hørte, og genoplever øjeblikket, hvor Macca angreb sin dyrepasser. Smith forklarer, at det er en del af hendes job at gribe ind i sådanne situationer, og understreger, at der altid er en ekstra dyrepasser til stede under krokodilleforestillinger. Jenkins, ejeren af Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo, fik revet sin tommelfinger af og pådrog sig hovedskader, da krokodillen greb ham og trak ham ned i vandet. Han blev fløjet til hospitalet og er i stabil tilstand. Smith brugte en pind til gentagne gange at slå krokodillen i hovedet, indtil den slap Jenkins fri. ‘Jeg prøvede bare at distrahere (krokodillen) for at give Ian og mig en chance for at komme væk derfra,’ sagde hun. Efter angrebet blev Jenkins, der er 58 år, fløjet til Bundaberg Base Hospital med en hovedskade. Han blev senere overført til Brisbane Hospital og har gennemgået adskillige timers kirurgi for at rekonstruere sin hånd. Hændelsen skete, da Jenkins forsøgte at tiltrække Maccas opmærksomhed med en kylling i sin højre hånd. Macca angreb uventet hans anden hånd og rev en del af hans venstre hånd ned til håndleddet. Jenkins undskyldte angiveligt over for paramedikerne for 'at være til besvær'. Den 58-årige krybdyrparkejer blev angrebet i Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo. Hans passion for krybdyr startede i hans barndom i Kenya, og han har været et respekteret medlem af lokalsamfundet i Childers i over 30 år. Dette er ikke den første alvorlige skade, Jenkins har pådraget sig i sit job. Fem år tidligere overlevede han et bid fra en østlig brun slange, og i 2003 blev han bidt af en kongebrun slange og to sorte slanger før det. I januar 2010, mens han forberedte en østlig brun slange til et show, blev han bidt gennem en pose, hvilket resulterede i kollaps og bevidsthedstab. Han modtog modgift og vendte tilbage til at optræde kort efter. Jenkins har boet i Australien i omkring 30 år og har stor viden om krybdyr. Hans kone, Barbara Jenkins, understreger, at han ikke opsøger fare, men er motiveret af sin passion for krybdyr og ønsket om at uddanne andre. Jenkins har udtrykt, at hans primære bekymring er hans familie og den nød, hans skader forårsager. Parken fungerede som sædvanligt dagen efter angrebet, bortset fra forestillingerne med krokodillefodring, som forventes at blive genoptaget, når Jenkins er kommet sig. Smith udtalte, at Macca normalt er rolig, og at den aggressive adfærd var usædvanlig. Hændelsen tjente dog som en stærk påmindelse om de iboende farer. Paramedikerne rykkede ud til zoologisk have kl. 12.55 lokal tid, ifølge en talsmand for Queensland Ambulance Service. Krokodilleangrebet fandt sted i Snakes Downunder Reptile Park and Zoo og kommer efter en nylig stigning i krokodilleangreb i Northern Territory.

article_content: Eva Schloss, whose mother later married Otto Frank, making her Anne Frank's stepsister after Anne's death in a concentration camp, reflects on her Holocaust experiences and the impact of Anne's legacy. At 15, Eva and her family were discovered hiding in Amsterdam, arrested by Nazis, and sent to Auschwitz. Eva and her mother survived, but her father and brother perished. Upon returning to Amsterdam, Eva's mother, Fritzi, married Otto Frank, the sole survivor of the Frank family, in 1953. Eva discussed her biography, 'After Auschwitz', on 'This Morning', exploring both the positive and negative effects of Anne's fame on her life. Anne and her sister Margot died from Typhus in Bergen-Belsen in 1945. After her diary was found in Amsterdam, Anne became a prominent Holocaust victim. While the world honored Anne, Eva struggled with living in her stepsister's shadow. Her new biography details this complex relationship. Eva shared that she knew Anne when they were 11, describing Anne as sophisticated and attention-seeking, even nicknamed 'Mrs Quack Quack' at school for talking too much. Both families were betrayed, Eva's by a Dutch nurse. The betrayer of the Frank family remains unknown. Eva recalled hearing about 'work camps' before her arrest but wasn't initially scared. However, arriving at Auschwitz changed everything. Auschwitz was filled with starvation, filth, and constant fear of selection. Survival meant staying alert and unnoticed. Eva showed her Auschwitz tattoo, a permanent reminder of her experiences. Eva initially believed her mother had died after seeing her led to the showers, but Fritzi survived and reunited with Eva in Amsterdam. Eva recounted her mother's marriage to Otto Frank and her subsequent introduction as 'Anne Frank's stepsister', a role she found challenging. She eventually accepted it, focusing on her own life and family, acknowledging that Anne had none of that. Eva also defended Justin Bieber's remark about Anne Frank being a 'Belieber', calling the criticism 'childish' and suggesting Anne would have been a fan. The full interview is available on the 'This Morning' website, and 'After Auschwitz' is available now.

Eva troede oprindeligt, at hendes mor var død, efter at have set hende blive ført til bruserne, men Fritzi overlevede og blev genforenet med Eva i Amsterdam. article_content: Louis van Gaal is eager to finalize discussions with Manchester United soon, as members of his prospective coaching staff require clarity regarding their roles with their current teams. Following the World Cup, Guus Hiddink will assume the position of head coach for Holland. Frank Hoek, Van Gaal's trusted goalkeeping coach, is expected to inform Hiddink today whether he intends to join Van Gaal at United or remain with the national team. A primary concern for Van Gaal is reportedly securing adequate funds to acquire three German players considered essential for Manchester United: Toni Kroos from Bayern Munich, along with Marco Reus and Mats Hummels, both currently with Borussia Dortmund. Despite ongoing speculation, senior figures at Manchester United are hesitant to immediately confirm Van Gaal as the permanent successor to David Moyes. They have suggested that it might be prudent to await the potential availability of a candidate such as Carlo Ancelotti. However, alternative sources anticipate an acceleration in the process, identifying Van Gaal as the leading contender, particularly after Ancelotti guided Real Madrid to the Champions League final. Manchester United is reportedly very interested in retaining interim player-manager Ryan Giggs and the 'Class of 92' – namely Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, and Phil Neville – within the future coaching structure, due to a belief that 'continuity is important'. While Van Gaal is keen to bring in his own team, including Hoek, the potential for disagreements during negotiations with Manchester United has been acknowledged. Sources close to Van Gaal in Holland suggest these issues are manageable, as Van Gaal recognizes the value of involving figures such as Giggs. The combined cost of acquiring his three German targets could exceed £100 million, even before factoring in other potential acquisitions such as Luke Shaw and Adam Lallana. This trio would represent a significant investment; however, the overall cost may be reduced if Shinji Kagawa were to return to Dortmund as part of any potential agreement. Kagawa initially transferred from the German club to United in June 2012. Van Gaal is keen for discussions to be concluded expeditiously, allowing him a brief period to formulate plans for the upcoming season at United before shifting his focus to Holland and the World Cup.

article_content: Reports indicate Sierra Leonean cyclist Mohamed Tholley is missing, occurring shortly after his teammate underwent Ebola testing. An athlete from Sierra Leone's Commonwealth Games delegation has reportedly disappeared. This follows concerns after a teammate was tested for the Ebola virus. Mohamed Tholley, the team's mountain biking champion, didn't appear for his scheduled time trial event in Glasgow. This absence has raised concerns. According to the Telegraph newspaper, Unisa Deen Kargbo, the Sierra Leone team's chef de mission, speculated that Mr. Tholley might be avoiding returning home due to the disease. He stated that one of their athletes was absent from his event and their whereabouts were unknown. He acknowledged the possibility of the athlete not returning, given the serious situation in their home country. Glasgow 2014 spokeswoman Jackie Brock-Doyle disputed these claims during a press briefing, saying they hadn't received reports of any missing athletes. She added that if an athlete were missing, it would be reported to them by concerned officials. This situation arose after another Sierra Leonean athlete at the Games, cyclist Moses Sesay, was hospitalized and isolated for four days for Ebola testing. Fortunately, he tested negative and competed in the road race time trial. Sesay expressed fear among athletes about returning home due to Ebola, hoping to remain in Britain until their Games visas expired. He comes from the Rotifunk Moyamba area, affected by the disease. He described feeling sick and tired, and the medical staff's protective suits made him very scared. He mentioned undergoing two Ebola tests, both negative, including one sent to London. After the London marathon earlier this year, Sierra Leonean runner Mami Konneh Lahun went missing after finishing in 20th place but was later found safe by police. Attempts to contact Sierra Leone team representatives for comments were unsuccessful. Sesay, a father of one, finished last in his race and arrived in Glasgow with his team the week before the Games. He fell ill shortly after attending the Opening Ceremony. Sesay said that all athletes were worried about returning home. He expressed a desire to stay in Britain, using the three-month visa obtained for the Games, due to the alarming situation back home. His mother and wife both work in the medical field. A West African official denied that another team member was missing or that others had been hospitalized. The official said Glasgow event authorities were communicating with the High Commission in London regarding the team's return schedule, and they still plan to participate in the Closing Ceremony. No special precautions had been implemented in the athlete's village. Moses Sesay has attended his second Commonwealth Games, having also competed in Delhi, India, four years prior. Officials confirmed there were no positive Ebola tests conducted in Scotland, while declining to comment about negative tests. Ebola is a severe illness affecting humans and primates. It's transmitted through contact with infected animals' bodily fluids. Once infected, it spreads through blood, urine, saliva, stools, and semen. The virus is fatal in up to 90% of cases, lacking a vaccine or known cure. Ebola causes sudden fever, weakness, muscle pain, headache, and sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, and impaired organ function. The incubation period spans two to 21 days, with contagion beginning upon symptom onset. In affected areas, or after contact with a suspected Ebola patient, seek medical help immediately. Treatment involves supportive care, like intravenous fluids, as there is no specific cure. Recovery is possible with appropriate care. Currently, there is no licensed Ebola vaccine available. The World Health Organisation monitors the situation and advises on travel restrictions when needed. The risk to travellers is low, as transmission requires direct contact with an infected person’s bodily fluids.

Virussen er dødelig i op til 90 % af tilfældene, og der findes ingen vaccine eller kur. Ebola forårsager pludselig feber, svaghed, muskelsmerter, hovedpine og ondt i halsen, efterfulgt af opkastning, diarré, udslæt og nedsat organfunktion. Behandlingen omfatter understøttende pleje som intravenøs væske, da der ikke findes en specifik kur. Helbredelse er mulig med den rette pleje. Der findes i øjeblikket ingen godkendt Ebola-vaccine. article_content: Yellowstone National Park's Steamboat Geyser surprised visitors with an eruption on Wednesday evening, its first in eight years. The geyser's outburst, lasting nine minutes from 7:30pm, sent water and steam soaring 300 feet into the air. Throughout the night, steam plumes continued to rise from the geyser. Steamboat is known as the most unpredictable geyser among the roughly 500 in Yellowstone, Wyoming. Its next eruption remains a mystery. Park rangers consider Steamboat a special geyser due to its unpredictable nature, making each eruption a highly anticipated event. In contrast, Old Faithful, Yellowstone's most famous geyser, is predictably timed. Steamboat is both the world's tallest and least reliable geyser. It erupted 29 times in 1969 but once remained dormant for 50 years, from 1911 to 1961. Eruptions can be months or years apart. Old Faithful, however, erupts with clockwork precision: approximately 91 minutes after a longer eruption or 65 minutes after a shorter one. Around 30 to 40 park visitors witnessed Steamboat's impressive display. Despite ongoing studies using instruments monitoring underground activity, scientists are still unsure of the exact cause of Steamboat's eruptions. Geologists explain that predictable geysers like Old Faithful are rare, with most being unpredictable. According to geologists, geysers like Old Faithful have a direct path from an underground chamber. Water and steam gather, and when the pressure exceeds a limit, steam forces water through the path into the air. Geysers, being rare natural phenomena, need specific geologic conditions such as hot springs and volcanoes to exist. Most geysers are located in five countries. Park geologist Hank Heasler noted that Yellowstone's geysers are sustained by an underground network where volcanic heat warms the water. However, the trigger for Steamboat's eruptions is still unknown to geologists. They have explored links to external forces, such as earthquakes, but have not found a correlation. Steamboat's last eruption occurred in 2005. Park officials reported that approximately 30 to 40 people witnessed Wednesday's eruption, describing a roar and ground shaking. Robb Long, a freelance photographer who saw the eruption, described it as an 'amazing experience,' sounding like a locomotive. Established in 1872, Yellowstone National Park, primarily located in Wyoming with parts in Idaho and Montana, contains about half of the world's geysers.
translated_content: Steamboat Gejseren i Yellowstone Nationalpark overraskede besøgende med et udbrud onsdag aften, det første i otte år. Gejserens udbrud, der varede ni minutter fra kl. 19.30, sendte vand og damp 90 meter op i luften. Dampfaner fortsatte med at stige op fra gejseren hele natten. Steamboat er kendt som den mest uforudsigelige gejser blandt de ca. 500 i Yellowstone, Wyoming. Dens næste udbrud er stadig et mysterium. Parkbetjente betragter Steamboat som en speciel gejser på grund af dens uforudsigelige natur, hvilket gør hvert udbrud til en længe ventet begivenhed. I modsætning hertil er Old Faithful, Yellowstones mest berømte gejser, forudsigeligt tidsbestemt. Steamboat er både verdens højeste og mindst pålidelige gejser. Den havde 29 udbrud i 1969, men lå engang i dvale i 50 år, fra 1911 til 1961. Der kan gå måneder eller år imellem udbruddene. Old Faithful går dog i udbrud med urværkspræcision: cirka 91 minutter efter et længerevarende udbrud eller 65 minutter efter et korterevarende. Omkring 30 til 40 parkgæster overværede Steamboats imponerende udbrud. På trods af løbende undersøgelser med instrumenter, der overvåger underjordisk aktivitet, er forskere stadig usikre på den præcise årsag til Steamboats udbrud. Geologer forklarer, at forudsigelige gejsere som Old Faithful er sjældne, og at de fleste er uforudsigelige. Ifølge geologer har gejsere som Old Faithful en direkte forbindelse fra et underjordisk kammer. Vand og damp ophobes, og når trykket overstiger en vis grænse, tvinger dampen vandet gennem forbindelsen op i luften. Gejsere, som er sjældne naturfænomener, kræver specifikke geologiske forhold som f.eks. varme kilder og vulkaner for at kunne eksistere. De fleste af verdens gejsere findes i fem lande. Parkgeolog Hank Heasler bemærkede, at Yellowstones gejsere forsynes af et underjordisk netværk, hvor vulkansk varme opvarmer vandet. Udløseren for Steamboats udbrud er dog stadig ukendt for geologer. De har undersøgt mulige sammenhænge med eksterne kræfter, såsom jordskælv, men har ikke fundet nogen klar sammenhæng. Steamboats seneste udbrud fandt sted i 2005. Parkbetjente rapporterede, at cirka 30 til 40 mennesker overværede onsdagens udbrud og beskrev en brølende lyd og en rysten i jorden. Robb Long, en freelancefotograf, der overværede udbruddet, beskrev det som en 'fantastisk oplevelse', der lød som et lokomotiv. Yellowstone Nationalpark, der blev etableret i 1872 og primært ligger i Wyoming med dele i Idaho og Montana, rummer omkring halvdelen af verdens gejsere.
